## Objective

Find either a smaller protein panel with comparable classification performance
or an alternative panel with improved performance. Compare it with the
in-class t-test/random-forest intersection followed by logistic regression.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(randomForest)
library(modelr)

load("../../data/biomarker-clean.RData")
```

## Reserving a test set

```{r split}
set.seed(101422)

part4_split <- initial_split(
  biomarker_clean,
  prop = 0.8,
  strata = group
)

part4_train <- training(part4_split)
part4_test <- testing(part4_split)

part4_train %>% count(group)
```

## 3. Establishing baseline from part 3

```{r}
source("part4baseline.R")
```


## 4. Using training-only to select our new smaller protein panel
```{r}
protein_names <- setdiff(
  names(part4_train),
  c("group", "ados")
)

part4_ranking <- purrr::map_dfr(protein_names, function(protein) {

  result <- t.test(
    part4_train[[protein]][part4_train$group == "ASD"],
    part4_train[[protein]][part4_train$group == "TD"]
  )

  tibble(
    protein = protein,
    p_value = result$p.value
  )
}) %>%
  arrange(p_value)
# choosing our proteins to start cross-validating
part4_ranking %>%
  slice_head(n = 3)
```
## 5. Using the top 3 proteins in cross validation
```{r}
set.seed(101422)

part4_folds <- vfold_cv(
  part4_train,
  v = 5,
  strata = group
)

evaluate_fold <- function(split) {

  fold_train <- analysis(split)
  fold_valid <- assessment(split)

  ranking <- purrr::map_dfr(protein_names, function(protein) {

    result <- t.test(
      fold_train[[protein]][fold_train$group == "ASD"],
      fold_train[[protein]][fold_train$group == "TD"]
    )

    tibble(
      protein = protein,
      p_value = result$p.value
    )
  }) %>%
    arrange(p_value)

  purrr::map_dfr(1:3, function(k) {

    selected <- head(ranking$protein, k)

    model_data <- fold_train %>%
      select(all_of(selected)) %>%
      mutate(class = fold_train$group == "ASD")

    model <- glm(
      class ~ .,
      data = model_data,
      family = binomial()
    )

    probabilities <- predict(
      model,
      newdata = fold_valid,
      type = "response"
    )

    tibble(
      panel_size = k,
      accuracy = mean(
        (probabilities > 0.5) == (fold_valid$group == "ASD")
      )
    )
  })
}

part4_cv_results <- part4_folds %>%
  mutate(scores = purrr::map(splits, evaluate_fold)) %>%
  select(id, scores) %>%
  unnest(scores)

part4_cv_summary <- part4_cv_results %>%
  group_by(panel_size) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_accuracy = mean(accuracy),
    sd_accuracy = sd(accuracy),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

part4_cv_summary
```



## 5. Final comparison

After choosing the alternative using training data, fit both final models
on the training set and evaluate on the same reserved test set. Report panel
size, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and ROC AUC. Define what counts as
comparable performance before inspecting final test results, and acknowledge
uncertainty from a single split.

## 6. Interpretation

To complete after evaluation: identify whether the alternative meets the
smaller-or-better objective. Do not assume an improvement before seeing results.
